text:
anya.m (marketing): Hey @sam.k / @jia.t — quick ask: we’re finalizing the webinar slides and want to cite live benchmark numbers. Can eng/runtime run one small sanity rerun and a reproducible full run with the exact methodology? Deadline = EOD in 3 days.

sam.k (eng/runtime): Sure. Which model and payloads? Also what metrics do you need? p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-token?

anya.m (marketing): Thanks. Primary asks: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, 99th tail for long requests, and per-token cost estimate for hosted vs dedicated. Model: please use the curated "redwood-13b-v1" quantized and float variants we showed in the deck. Payloads: small (1–8 tokens), medium (32–128), and long (512). Provide sample sizes and seed for reproducibility.

jia.t (eng/runtime): Ok. For long (512) we need to confirm KV caching and attention optimizations are on. Do you want warm-cache numbers (steady-state) or cold-start?

carlos.p (marketing): Warm-cache steady-state preferred for audience-facing numbers. But include a short note on cold-starts as a footnote.

sam.k (eng/runtime): Got it. Plan: smoke run (fast) to confirm configs, then full runs with N=500 samples per bucket. Will run both quantized (q4/8) and float fp16 variants. Need an input set — do you have canonical prompts or should we randomize from public prompts?

anya.m (marketing): Use canonical prompts: I've uploaded a compressed payload to s3://redwood-marketing/bench/2026-03-18/bench_inputs.jsonl.gz — please use that and the same random seed of `42` so we can reproduce. Add a README line in the artifact with the seed and exact command.

sam.k (eng/runtime): Thanks. One more: what concurrency/batch sizes should we benchmark? We can do single-request latency and batch size 8/16 throughput runs. Recommend we capture both.

anya.m (marketing): Yes — single-request (latency) and batch 8/16 throughput. Also collect memory/GPU utilization charts and a short flamegraph if possible.

jia.t (eng/runtime): Will do. I'll run `./bench/run_bench.sh --model redwood-13b-v1 --inputs s3://redwood-marketing/bench/... --seed 42 --variants fp16,q4_0 --batches 1,8,16 --samples 500` and upload artifacts to the same s3 prefix + `artifacts/runtime/`.

runtime-bot: CI job triggered: bench-job-1782501123-smoke (queued).

sam.k (eng/runtime): Smoke done — quick note: quantized q4_0 has a tokenization edge-case for prompts with trailing newlines; I patched tokenizer config in the run. Will note in artifact. Full runs queued; estimate 6 hours. Prioritizing the warm-cache steady-state numbers.

anya.m (marketing): Great — could you include raw CSV + a one-slide PNG summary (3 bars: p50/p95/tokens-per-sec) so design can drop into the deck?

sam.k (eng/runtime): Yep. Will include `summary-slide.png` and `raw-results.csv`. Also adding a small markdown `methodology.md` with command lines and configs.

carlos.p (marketing): Thanks team! If anything blocks, ping in #marketing and I'll escalate. :pray:

sam.k (eng/runtime): Upload complete. Artifacts: s3://redwood-marketing/bench/2026-03-18/artifacts/runtime/bench-job-1782501123/ — contains `raw-results.csv`, `summary-slide.png`, `methodology.md`, `notes.txt` (contains tokenizer patch note and warm vs cold numbers).

jia.t (eng/runtime): Quick sanity: p95 for q4_0 on long (512) looks ~18% slower vs fp16 due to KV packing overhead in this workload. Logged in notes.

anya.m (marketing): Perfect — we'll use fp16 as headline with a callout about q4 tradeoffs and link to the artifact for full transparency. Thanks so much.

sam.k (eng/runtime): If you want a rerun with different burst policies or a region-specific check (eu-west), say the word; can queue it.

anya.m (marketing): Not for the first cut. Maybe after the press release. Appreciate it. :rocket:
